_why: One versioned statement of what each box offers the pool, so a supervisor on any box can be started by an identical command line and the shape of the fleet is a file somebody can read rather than three hand-typed invocations nobody wrote down. Values here are the ones the loops were observed running on 2026-09-03; changing the fleet means changing this file. Raised 2026-09-04 against measurement, not intuition: see _measured_2026_09_04.

gx10-6b77._alias_why: The OS hostname is now sparklina. The supervisor resolves this explicit alias to the same shape; both names remain placement tags for existing submissions.

_measured_2026_09_04: Both GB10 boxes are 121 GB unified. sparklina announced 40 of them and one GPU slot, and its only GPU token was held by a legitimate long out-of-pool encode drawing 14 W of a ~140 W envelope -- so a queued GPU action waited 30 minutes on a box that was, by power, one tenth loaded, with 111 GB available and load 3.0 across 10 cores. gpu-slots 1 -> 2, mem-gb 40 -> 80. sparky was the mirror case on memory alone: 96 GB available behind a 48 GB offer, so its 40 GB queue head could not pair with anything; mem-gb 48 -> 72, and gpu-slots stays 2 because load was already 14.5 across 10 cores and GPU concurrency, not memory, is what serialises that box. The caps stay well under available memory on purpose: the offer is the admission bound that keeps concurrent agent compute from taking a box down.  Later, 06:35: gx10-6b77 held both GPU tokens while one-tenth loaded -- 111 GB of 121 available, load 2.65 across 20 cores, GPU drawing 13.9 W of a ~140 W envelope, one token being the out-of-pool ts60 encode, which is single-stream and does not fill the box.  A token prices an envelope nobody measures, and at 2 it read 'full' with the SMs idle: a queued 12-minute suite waited ten minutes for a machine that could have run three of it.  gpu-slots 2 -> 3 on that measurement.  sparky stays at 2, its load already 14.5 across 10 cores.
_capacity_policy_2026_09_05: All three hosts expose their full inherited CPU affinity to admitted jobs. Rob requires available capacity to serve independent test/GPU work; preferred-core-only pinning left ten usable ARM cores outside the pool. CPU slots count logical CPUs, not equivalent performance; measurements still declare host class and isolation. Memory and GPU budgets retain their measured bounds.
